activity.title: Stage 07 React TypeScript state, effects, routes, and delivery evidence
activity.instructions:
This bounded activity maps to DotNet-React-Roadmap/7.md. Complete Stage 05
and the Stage 06 JavaScript/TypeScript API page first. It is a guided
learner-attestation task, not a full Stage 07 or deployment approval.

Work in a learner-owned scratch React project with learning data only. Read
package.json and the existing entry file before editing. Keep the API base
URL in the local environment or an explicit proxy; VITE_ variables are
shipped to the browser and must never contain secrets. Record the actual
frontend/API origins and CORS or proxy choice without credentials.

Split the page into components such as ExpenseForm, ExpenseList, Summary,
and App. Use stable keys, props/callbacks, controlled fields, immutable
updates, functional updaters when based on old state, and the shared
categoryId request/categoryName response contract. Record a real submit,
empty state, and validation boundary, or the exact blocker.

Use useEffect only for the external API synchronization. Model idle/loading/
ready/error states, abort on cleanup, handle AbortError separately, include
reactive dependencies, and runtime-check unknown JSON before setting state.
Record actual loading, empty, success, error, and cleanup observations;
StrictMode development behavior is not proof of production request counts.

Add a route/layout boundary for expense and category views, a small Context
only where shared state needs it, and an error boundary for render errors.
Keep async event/effect errors separate from render error boundaries. Record
the URL-not-found route behavior and any state lifting/Context rerender
decision. Do not add a state library without a concrete pain point.

Finish with accessible UX and a delivery note: focus/labels/keyboard and
understandable status messages, actual API 201/400/401/404/500 or network
observations where tested, a real build result if run, environment-specific
API origin/HTTPS/refresh-route assumptions, and one click-to-response trace.
If any tool or browser path is unavailable, report it as incomplete rather
than asserting a successful test or deployment.

A recorded blocker preserves an honest incomplete result; it does not earn the point for the corresponding unperformed observation. Complete each positive rubric item only with actual evidence.
activity.expected_output: A learner evidence note with component/props/state boundaries, actual effect cleanup and fetch-state observations, route/context/error-boundary behavior, accessible UX and API checks, build/config evidence, and explicit blockers.

rubric.evidence: The note identifies component responsibilities, controlled form fields, immutable or functional updates, stable list keys, and the shared API contract from actual code. Missing or blocked required evidence remains incomplete and earns no point.

rubric.criterion: Effect, cancellation, and runtime data evidence
rubric.evidence: The note records real idle/loading/ready/error and cleanup or AbortError behavior, dependency choices, and runtime validation of unknown API JSON. Missing or blocked required evidence remains incomplete and earns no point.

rubric.criterion: Routes, shared state, and error behavior
rubric.evidence: The note records route/layout and URL-not-found behavior, a justified lifting or Context choice, and the separate render versus async error handling paths. Missing or blocked required evidence remains incomplete and earns no point.

The note records observed keyboard/focus/status behavior, API outcomes, build/config and origin assumptions, and one click-to-response trace without claiming unrun browser or deployment results. Missing or blocked required evidence remains incomplete and earns no point.
